summary: Escalating Middle East conflicts and Red Sea disruptions drove crude oil prices past $100 per barrel and pushed supertanker rates to record highs, severely straining global supply chain margins across Asia. This severe energy volatility placed heavy pressure on regional currencies like the Indian Rupee, triggering central bank interventions and emergency freight surcharges on ocean shipping. In response, both India and China are doubling down on structural resilience—India through its new Integrated Transport and Logistics Authority and refiner forex support, and China by expanding alternative overland rail corridors and non-Western financial rails like CIPS. Looking ahead, persistent geopolitical friction will keep ocean freight costs elevated, accelerating state intervention in energy security and driving trade flows toward bypass transit routes.
